The #COVID19 pandemic has increased the number of people experiencing anxiety/depression to 4 in 10 people.

My bill lifts the IMD exclusion and will make it easier for patients to seek the mental health treatment they need. #MentalHealthAwarenessMonth

Today is National Cancer Survivors Day. Millions of survivors have life-long lymphedema as a result of their cancer treatment and it’s important that they know they are not being left behind. This is why I am supporter of the #LymphedemaTreatmentAct https://t.co/17HgmR0xDZ

Last week was National Cancer Survivor Awareness Day. @RepBuddyCarter is making sure Congress can support cancer survivors after their treatment. A chronic illness like Lymphedema can take over one’s life. We need to do everything we can to support them. https://t.co/4Czwf22pS9

In the majority opinion, Justice Thomas stated: "We know of no other constitutional right that an individual may exercise only after demonstrating to government officers some special need."
No right is lesser than another. Today's decision reflects that fact.

BREAKING: The FDA has approved the first gene therapy to treat adults with Hemophilia B. This is a huge milestone in Hemophilia treatment. I am thankful for this new, safe, and effective treatment option.

This month is National Parkinson's Awareness Month. Nearly 90K Americans are diagnosed with this neurodegenerative disorder every year and it's important to know the signs and symptoms for early detection. Learn more: https://t.co/8C70CtU7X2
Yes, we can all agree Parkinson's Disease sucks. I'm sorry to hear of my friend and fellow Budget Committee member's diagnosis. My prayers are with @RepWexton and her family.

.@SecBecerra's comparison of America's treatment of UACs to an assembly line shows how broken our immigration system really is. With the Biden Admin's open border policies, the system has become astonishingly cruel and inhumane. https://t.co/fvNGgVriDH

Today, Susan Rice will depart from her role as domestic policy advisor to @POTUS before she makes our border crisis even worse. The Biden Administration’s policies have led to the inhumane treatment of migrants and exploitation of minors.  https://t.co/jfmhlcnnUn

During a 2016 @HouseCommerce hearing, an advocate for sickle cell told us no new FDA-approved treatment had been developed in 40 years. This jarring statement underscored the consequences of inaction and emphasized the urgent need for to address this debilitating disease. https://t.co/I4dSZxLPjl
Empowering patients with personalized care is essential, and compounded hormone therapies are a crucial part of it. I joined @RepWexton to urge the @US_FDA to safeguard treatment access.

Great to meet Millie Echols, a fellow North Texan, at the Children's Hospital Association Family Advocacy Day. Diagnosed with ASD at just 18 months old, Millie now selflessly collects and donates stuffed animals to children undergoing treatment. Keep up the great work, Millie! https://t.co/6mFXNiVC3O

Sickle cell is the most common inherited blood disorder in the U.S., yet we still do not have preventive treatments. 

We must prioritize funding for research and investment into better treatment options for individuals who are suffering. https://t.co/e0TJahtUDE
.@HouseBudgetGOP's budget PRESERVES and PROTECTS Medicare and Social Security.
This budget not only strengthens Medicare, but also strengthens the doctor-patient relationship because every American deserves access to affordable and personalized care. https://t.co/VCHp9mbRzI

For nearly 40 years, progress in sickle cell treatment was almost stagnant. To raise awareness, I joined with @RepDannyDavis and @RepBuddyCarter to introduce a resolution to designate September as #SickleCellAwarenessMonth.

A builder can open his own construction business, a lawyer can open his own firm - why can’t a doctor own his own hospital? 
https://t.co/EBxOy5mGF2

The current Medicare fee schedule is unsustainable and unpredictable. 

I introduced the Provider Reimbursement Stability Act of 2023 to help doctors keep caring for American seniors. https://t.co/pieUOR45MO

The proposed 3.4% cut to Medicare payments spells disaster for physicians nationwide. In an op-ed for @WashTimes, the @GOPDoctors sheds light on the impending crisis and our fight to preserve the doctor patient relationship.  
https://t.co/D1xz6I4vED

I Introduced the GOLD Card Act with @RepGonzalez to free qualifying providers from burdensome prior authorization hurdles. This legislation would help physicians deliver timely, quality care. https://t.co/eeBlbGAoJO

My bill to lift the IMD exclusion, as part of the SUPPORT Act, passed the House in December. This legislation aims to modernize Medicaid coverage of addiction treatment in Institutes for Mental Diseases and directly addresses the fentanyl crisis in the US, which is linked to rising drug addiction and homelessness. https://t.co/IWTUffy4ut

On January 1st, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) cut payments by 3.4% to physicians for services rendered to Medicare patients.

As physicians, we cannot simply stand by and allow that to happen.

It's crucial sickle cell disease patients have access to care coordination & treatments needed to combat the disease. 

I introduced the Sickle Cell Disease Comprehensive Care Act to provide patients access to health home services to manage their symptoms. https://t.co/0UYEXvktXI

The Creating Hope Reauthorization Act would extend the FDA’s authority to issue Priority Review Vouchers to encourage treatment for rare pediatric diseases.

I co-lead this bill to ensure rare disease patients have access to future medications. https://t.co/1cZnPaMaNN

The passage of the Preventing Maternal Deaths Reauthorization Act will protect mothers from future maternal health disparities.

This is a huge win for maternal healthcare in the U.S. See my statement ⬇️ https://t.co/jraKfxVino
